messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Reynolds <alice@medsys.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt/output PII: acceptance checkpoints & residency confirmation

Hi Alice — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few acceptance checkpoints so procurement/security can sign off: 

- What we discussed: Medsys will send patient-facing prompts and clinician notes to Redwood for inference. The two items you asked us to confirm: (1) which artifacts are persisted (raw prompts, model outputs, chat transcripts, model metadata/logs), and (2) where those artifacts live and for how long.

- Redwood capability summary (high-level):
  • Prompts/outputs: configurable — can be flagged no_store, or persisted for a TTL.
  • Audit logs/trace: available, can be retained per-customer.
  • Residency: hosted regions in eu-west-1 (Frankfurt) and eu-central-1 available; Dedicated/Private deployments give full regional control.
  • Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+, at-rest encryption; Dedicated/Private can use customer KMS (BYOK).

Ask: could you confirm the following acceptance criteria from your security team?
  1) Are raw prompts allowed to be stored at all, or must they be no_store/ephemeral?
  2) Minimum retention window for audit traces and aggregated metrics (e.g., 30 days, 1 year, 7 years)?
  3) Residency requirement (Frankfurt vs other EU region) and whether BYOK is mandatory.

I attached a lightweight PII acceptance matrix (pii_acceptance_matrix.csv) and an initial redlines draft for legal (redlines_draft.docx) — both are just starting points.

Proposed next steps if that looks right to you: technical workshop (we'll bring Marissa + infra) to lock config, followed by a short procurement/sox packet for your team. Can you share who from security/procurement we should include?

Thanks — Sean

From: Alice Reynolds <alice@medsys.io>

Subject: Re: Prompt/output PII: acceptance checkpoints & residency confirmation

Thanks, Sean — good recap. A few clarifications from our side after a quick sync with security/procurement: 

1) Raw prompts: security prefers raw prompts to be marked no_store by default. We do want the option to persist specific training/test prompts for up to 3 years, but only if we explicitly opt in and the data is pseudonymized.

2) Audit traces: must be retained for 7 years for certain audit scopes (billing and compliance side) — however, we can scope that to meta-level traces (request id, timestamp, model version, token counts). Full request payloads should not be retained for 7 years.

3) Residency: EU residency is mandatory; primary region preference is eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). BYOK: preferred for any at-rest retention beyond 90 days. For hosted options, procurement asks for documentation on encryption key management and whether BYOK can be supported in a hosted mode or only in Dedicated/Private.

Please include a short paragraph that we can hand to our legal team explaining the difference between: a) hosted default (short TTL + optional no_store), b) Dedicated w/ BYOK (longer retention), c) Private/on-prem. Procurement is copied — they will want to see the redlines.

On scheduling: please propose 1-hour tech workshop windows next week (CEST mornings preferred).

Best,
Alice Reynolds
Director of Security Programs
Medsys Health
alice@medsys.io

Hi Alice — Marissa from Solutions here. Quick technical clarifications and what we can deliver out of the box vs configuration items: 

- No_store flag: supported. When set, prompts and outputs are not written to durable storage; ephemeral caches (KV cache) remain in-memory for the session and can be dropped on session end.

- Retention windows: Hosted Redwood default audit/log retention = 30 days for request payloads and 90 days for aggregated telemetry. Hosted can be configured to extend telemetry retention but raw payload retention beyond 30 days typically requires Dedicated or Private.

- BYOK / Customer KMS:
  • Hosted: we offer a managed encryption service; we can perform limited BYOK integration for certain enterprise agreements but full BYOK where keys never leave the customer account is available on Dedicated and Private.
  • Dedicated: you can provide a KMS key in your cloud account and we will encrypt at-rest with that key.
  • Private/on-prem: full customer-side key management (HSM/KMS) is supported.

- 7-year audit requirement: we recommend splitting traces into two classes: (A) metadata-only audit trails (request id, ts, model id, token counts, status) which can be exported and retained for 7 years to customer storage (S3 or equivalent) and (B) full payloads which remain no_store or short TTL (30d) unless explicit opt-in. We can provide an automated export job that writes metadata-only logs into your S3 bucket daily (encrypted with your key) for long-term retention.

- Residency: we can deploy the inference endpoint in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For Hosted customers requiring strict EU-only residency + BYOK + long retention, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path.

I attached a residency matrix (residency_matrix.pdf) that shows tradeoffs and where each artifact can live. If you confirm no_store for raw prompts and accept metadata-only exports for long-term audit, we can scope the procurement docs quickly.

Proposed tech workshop agenda (30–60m):
  1) Walk through pii_acceptance_matrix (what gets no_store vs persisted)
  2) Residency/KMS options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
  3) Export workflows for long-term metadata retention (S3 + BYOK)
  4) Next steps & procurement packet

Suggested windows (CEST): Wed 23 Jul 09:00–11:00 or Thu 24 Jul 09:00–11:00. Let me know which works.

Thanks — Marissa

Alice / procurement — great, thanks for the clarifications. Quick summary and proposed commitments so legal/procurement have a short handoff paragraph: 

Summary commitments:
- Raw prompts: default = no_store. Customer can opt-in to explicit prompt persistence, which must be pseudonymized and documented.
- Audit traces: metadata-only traces (request id, timestamp, model id, token counts, status) can be exported daily to your S3 with customer-managed encryption for 7-year retention.
- Hosted vs Dedicated/Private: Hosted supports short TTLs and limited BYOK; Dedicated/Private required for full BYOK and long-term raw payload retention.
- Residency: we will deploy endpoints in eu-central-1 for Medsys.

Next steps:
1) Tech workshop (30–60m) to finalize configuration and export details — proposed slot: Wed 23 Jul 2025, 09:30 CEST.
2) Redwood to deliver a short one-page summary for legal describing differences among Hosted / Dedicated / Private for procurement (we will attach redlines_draft.docx).
3) Procurement to confirm any additional contract redlines; we'll iterate.

If that looks good, procurement can pick the workshop slot (23 Jul 09:30 CEST is our first choice). If Medsys needs different timing, Sean will re-propose.

Thanks — talk soon.
